title: Anime look trial: six shader tricks at the plaza fountain
question: Which of the six tricks should we keep, and should the look go to every place?

media.caption: Your reference (art/refs/style/anime-fountain-reference.png). You asked: "There isnt like some shader tricks and texture hacks we can to to approach this look is there?", then "Yeah lets try it I say". Everything below is a screenshot of the real game at the plaza fountain, nothing painted. The trial is six tricks behind a URL flag, so the game you play now is unchanged: ?anime=1 turns all six on, and a list turns on some of them, for example ?anime=toon,outline. 1 toon: the sun's light in three tones (lit, a middle band, shade) with a soft edge between them; the shade side goes cool blue and a little richer in colour instead of grey, the lit side a touch warm. It changes with the time of day. 2 outline: thin lines on edges and outlines, drawn as a darker shade of the colour underneath, never black, fading out in the distance. 3 dapple: under tree crowns the shadow becomes leaf shade with spots of sun in it. 4 paint: walls and stone a little darker at the foot and lighter up top, and a faint colour drift over stone and paving. 5 water: new fountain water, turquoise by depth, ripple rings, foam where the water lands, sparkles, the falling water as separate streams with splash rings. 6 crowns: tree crowns and hedges shaded as soft clumps instead of flat facets. An earlier style study (cel shading with ink lines, 2026-09-29) got "looks more like evening", so here the shade is lifted and kept cool rather than dark.

Each trick on its own, phone, after work. Phone cost, measured at 390x844 on quality medium as phones run it (rendering at 585x1266), same spot, on this machine's GPU, median of 40 frames: now 92 draw calls, 159k triangles, 4.0 ms a frame. toon 94 calls, 159k, 4.5 ms. outline 93, 159k, 5.4 ms (one extra full-screen pass, no extra scene draw). dapple 92, 159k, 4.0 ms (one 256x256 map). paint 93, 159k, 5.0 ms. water 91, 159k, 5.1 ms (three meshes in place of five, 870 triangles). crowns 94, 160k, 4.7 ms (no cost while playing, a moment at load). All six 92, 160k, 5.8 ms morning and 6.4 ms after work against 4.1 ms now. So no extra draw calls or triangles to speak of (the 1 to 3 call differences are passers-by walking in and out of view); the price is shader work per pixel, about half as much again per frame, mostly the outline, the paint and the water. The desktop numbers move the same way but are lost in this machine's noise (7 to 10 ms either way).

options.label: toon
options.note: Three-tone light, cool shade, warm lit side. Left now, right ?anime=toon. About +0.5 ms on a phone.

options.label: outline
options.note: Coloured edge lines. Left now, right ?anime=outline. About +1 ms on a phone.

options.label: dapple
options.note: Leaf shade with sun spots under crowns. Left now, right ?anime=dapple. No measurable cost.

options.label: paint
options.note: Darker feet, lighter tops, faint colour drift on stone and paving. Left now, right ?anime=paint. About +1 ms on a phone.

options.label: water
options.note: Stylised fountain water with streams and splash rings. Left now, right ?anime=water. About +1 ms on a phone.

options.label: crowns
options.note: Soft clump shading on crowns and hedges. Left now, right ?anime=crowns. No cost while playing.

options.label: rollout: make the kept tricks the default everywhere
options.note: Pick this as well if the tricks you keep should become the game's look in every place, not only a flag.

decision: rollout, "just fix the fountain"; toon kept; dapple and crowns dropped
